counterfactual_missing_items: normal laboratory studies, including complete blood count, coagulation profile, and gene sequencing
no family history of bleeding disorders or stroke
decisive_items: fetal MRI at 25 weeks, which showed a 2.3 cm porencephalic cyst in the right frontotemporal–insular region
Cranial ultrasound on day 1 showed a right porencephalic area
Fetal ultrasound at 20 weeks suggested intracranial hemorrhage
response.rationale: R8 is the most likely diagnosis due to the presence of a porencephalic cyst and porencephalic area, which are characteristic features of porencephaly. R4 is a close runner-up, as intracranial hemorrhage is suggested by fetal ultrasound and may have contributed to the development of the porencephalic cyst.

rejected.why: micropolygyria is a feature of the condition, but not the primary diagnosis
microcephaly is a symptom, but not the primary diagnosis
congenital CMV infection is possible, but not supported by IgM negative results
genetic disorder is possible, but not supported by normal gene sequencing and metabolic screening
